minutes.headline: School Committee held the FY16 budget hearing on a level service budget and voted to appoint a diversity advisory committee.
minutes.summary: The meeting opened with the public hearing on the FY16 level service school budget, with residents questioning salaries, special education, insurance, school choice and class sizes. The committee then heard a school building committee report, appointed a diversity advisory committee, and scheduled joint meetings with the reuse committee. In public comment the board discussed whether to seek an override next year, and residents challenged earlier statements that the new building would not raise operating costs.

public_comment.topic: Clarifying questions on salaries, SPED contingency, non-resident revenue, insurance, headcount and curriculum adoption.
Asked for explanation of master teacher and high school retirement longevity lines and the secretary line.
Concern that a level budget cannot cover rising non-academic costs without hurting class sizes and staff; would support a larger budget.
Asked about guidance counselor lines and small high school elective classes versus larger 4th and 6th grade classes.
Level service versus level funded; staffing ratio chart through FY14 and 7 FTE added in FY15; enrollment trends.
Suggested ways to fund two teachers: SPED contingency, insurance, school choice; also criticized paraprofessional value.
Asked the committee to consider expanding school choice to elementary grades.
Charter timing of budget presentation; said she was told the new school would not need more staff.
Said he was told no additional operating costs for the new building; would not support an override.
Staffing costs growing faster than revenue; wants multi-year projections; asked about longevity cap.
Thanked organizers of the volunteer recognition event.

votes.motion: Adopt the slate of diversity advisory committee appointments.

budget_items.topic: Level service budget vs town manager recommendation
budget_items.what_was_said: The school budget is above the town manager's recommended budget by a stated gap; the town manager proposed using one-time funds for instructional materials.
Choice brought money in FY15 and is expected to fall next year.

budget_items.topic: Special education and Title I grants
budget_items.what_was_said: SPED grant and Title I expected next year.
Loss of non-resident tuition and the state kindergarten grant were moved into the operating budget.
Renewal came in well above the hoped-for increase.
A contingency sits in the private placements line in the level service budget.

budget_items.topic: Teacher positions funded from tuition savings
budget_items.what_was_said: Two teachers were funded from tuition savings, said to reduce out-of-district costs.
Contractual stipends and longevity payments explained.
A resident listed possible savings from teachers, SPED contingency, insurance and choice.

budget_items.topic: Gap between level service and town manager funds
budget_items.what_was_said: Superintendent and a member discussed the remaining gap if one-time funds come in.
Cost to educate a student versus choice revenue received.

decisions.decision: Members agreed to offer the 9th, 16th and 30th of April at 7 p.m. or later for a joint meeting with the building reuse committee, to be conveyed to its chair.
No line item transfers were presented this evening.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted to adopt the slate of diversity advisory committee appointments.
The committee held the FY16 budget hearing on a level service budget, which sits above the town manager's recommended budget by a stated gap.
Residents questioned salaries, special education, health insurance, school choice and class sizes before the hearing closed.
Members agreed to offer three April dates for a joint meeting with the building reuse committee, to be conveyed to its chair.
The board discussed a possible override next year without resolution, and residents challenged earlier statements that the new building would add no operating costs.

why_it_matters: The gap between the level service school budget and the town manager's recommendation bears on whether class sizes and staffing hold, and on whether residents are asked to vote on an override.
Residents' questions about the new building's operating costs touch what the school will add to the town budget, mostly taxes, in later years.
watch_next: Joint meeting with the building reuse committee, offered for the 9th, 16th or 30th of April at 7 p.m. or later.
Any decision on whether to seek an override next year, which the board left unresolved.
